notes: The codebook underwent language rewording while maintaining its original structure and level of detail to ensure consistent annotation quality.

codes.name: access barriers
codes.definition: Physical obstacles that hinder patients from accessing care, including distance, transportation, scheduling, language, and paperwork challenges.
codes.clarification: This includes any factor that prevents a patient from reaching care, such as no nearby clinic or inability to navigate the system.
codes.negative_clarification: NOT the price of care itself — that is "cost concerns". A long delay once you already have an appointment is "wait times".

positive_examples.text: The nearest clinic is two bus transfers away and I can't get there without taking a full day off work.
positive_examples.why: Distance and transport physically block reaching care.

negative_examples.text: I finally saw the doctor but the copay was more than I could afford.
negative_examples.why: The obstacle here is price, which is cost concerns, not access.

codes.name: cost concerns
codes.definition: Worry about the monetary price of care — bills, copays, premiums, or fear of debt.
codes.clarification: Include any mention of affordability, insurance not covering enough, or skipping care because of money.
codes.negative_clarification: NOT difficulty physically reaching care (that is "access barriers"), even though both can stop someone from being seen.

positive_examples.text: I skipped the follow-up because I couldn't afford another $200 visit.
positive_examples.why: Care was forgone specifically because of its price.

negative_examples.text: I couldn't get an appointment for three months.
negative_examples.why: This is a scheduling delay (wait times), with no mention of money.

codes.name: provider trust
codes.definition: The patient's confidence in, or distrust of, their clinician or the health system.
codes.clarification: Include feeling heard or dismissed, doubting a diagnosis, or relying on a provider's judgment.
codes.negative_clarification: NOT general satisfaction with logistics like cost or wait times; this is about the relationship and credibility of the provider.

positive_examples.text: My doctor never listens, so I've started ignoring the advice I'm given.
positive_examples.why: Expresses distrust in the provider relationship.

negative_examples.text: The waiting room was crowded and I sat there for an hour.
negative_examples.why: A logistics complaint (wait times), not about trust in the provider.

codes.name: wait times
codes.definition: Delay between seeking care and receiving it — appointment lead time or time spent waiting on the day.
codes.clarification: Include long lead times for appointments and long in-clinic waits.
codes.negative_clarification: NOT being unable to reach the clinic at all (that is "access barriers"); wait times assume care is reachable but slow.

positive_examples.text: The first available appointment was four months out.
positive_examples.why: A direct delay in receiving care.

negative_examples.text: There's no specialist within a hundred miles of me.
negative_examples.why: Care is unreachable, an access barrier, not merely delayed.
